Question four. What is the logical order of sequel clause execution? Not the order you write it. From and joins first, then WHERE, GROUP BY and HAVING. Then SELECT, which is where window functions are computed, with qualify right after. Then DISTINCT, ORDER BY and LIMIT. So WHERE can't see a row number, or any name made up in SELECT: neither exists yet. ORDER BY runs later, so it can. Question five. What is the difference between WHERE and HAVING? Watch twenty-four orders go through. WHERE keeps the eleven over a hundred dollars, row by row. GROUP BY makes four regions. HAVING keeps the two over four hundred. Put a sum in WHERE instead, and DuckDB refuses: the aggregate doesn't exist yet. So filter rows in WHERE whenever you can, and there are fewer rows to group. Keep HAVING for conditions on an aggregate. Window functions have one more setting that trips people up: the frame.

Question six. What is a window frame, and what is the difference between rows and range? The frame is the set of rows the function sees for the current one. Here, two payments land on the same day. Rows counts physical rows, so the running total climbs one payment at a time: a hundred, three fifty, four twenty-five. Range goes by the order by value, so both payments on the second come in together, and both get four twenty-five. Rows is the predictable one. Reach for range when tied values belong together, or when the frame is a span of time. That last case is the next question.
